title: The pigeonhole principle over a finite set, in refutation form
statement: Let s and t be finite sets over the naturals and g a function on the naturals. If the size of t is strictly less than the size of s, and g sends every member of s to a member of t, then g is NOT injective on the members of s -- assuming it is yields a contradiction.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.pigeonhole : ((x0 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x1 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x3 : AxNat.lt (AxNat.Finset.card x1) (AxNat.Finset.card x0)) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x4) Bool.true) -> Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x1 (x2 x4)) Bool.true))) -> ((x5 : ((x5 : AxNat) -> ((x6 : AxNat) -> ((x7 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x5) Bool.true) -> ((x8 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x6) Bool.true) -> ((x9 : Eq.{1} AxNat (x2 x5) (x2 x6)) -> Eq.{1} AxNat x5 x6)))))) -> False))))))

evidence.supports: The statement says what its name says -- checked at a concrete instance with hand-computed numerals and paired with the specific wrong statement it rules out
evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell a THEOREM's statement is not what its name says: a `card_le_of_injOn` with its two `card`s transposed, an `exists_collision` whose pair need not be DISTINCT, or a `pigeonhole` whose strict inequality points the other way would each be admitted, carry an empty axiom footprint, and pass every other row in this ledger. `nat_prelude/finset_pigeonhole_tests.rs` instantiates each statement at a concrete pair of sets whose cardinalities are computed independently, and pairs every positive with the wrong statement it rules out. Three of its controls are the sharper kind, where a hypothesis cannot be DISCHARGED (`infer` must fail) rather than a conclusion merely being false.

notes: Three lines from F:nat-finset-card-le-of-injon: the injection bounds card s by card t, Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le chains that with the strict inequality to card t < card t, and Nat.lt_irrefl closes. This is the REFUTATION form, which is the strongest form whose statement needs no search; F:nat-finset-exists-collision produces the explicit colliding pair and pays for it with a bounded one.
